A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same federated-learning governance research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reformulation and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original numerical simulations of sanction thresholds, participation dynamics, coalition stability and information design in Sections 5–10.

after.justification: v2 reports original stylized simulations and a Fashion-MNIST federated experiment in Section 7, with additional qualitative robustness results in Appendix D.3.

M1.justification: v1 specifies curvature-based reward alignment, orthogonal sanctions and cost-aware/adaptive audit procedures. v2 replaces these detailed prescriptions with generic violation-score penalties, adds scenario/log-based index estimation, and centers audit allocation on cardinality-constrained client selection. Greedy allocation, mixed evaluation and warning-based switching remain.

E1.justification: v2 adds Fashion-MNIST image classification, including head-focused client gaming and hidden tail-class welfare evaluation. This introduces an actual dataset and learning task beyond v1's stylized numerical models. The stylized evidence also shifts toward fixed honest/gaming client populations.

E2.justification: Neither version reports head-to-head benchmarking against competing FL or audit-allocation methods. Named robust-aggregation methods remain related-work or design discussions; FedAvg in v2 serves as the training protocol. Changes to behavioral scenarios and design parameters are experimental-setting changes.

E3.justification: v2 replaces analytic grids and participation trajectories with post-burn-in scenario averages and revised penalty/public-weight sweeps. Its new FL protocol uses 30 clients, 40 rounds, full participation, 30% gaming clients, separate head-validation/tail-test metrics, and averages over the last ten rounds. These are new protocols, not comparable reruns of v1.

E4.justification: v1's alignment-angle, information-delay, participation-threshold, coalition-externality and sample-requirement analyses disappear. v2 reports different penalty and information-weight sensitivity studies, plus Fashion-MNIST checks varying gaming fractions to 20%/40%, class assignments, seeds and training hyperparameters. Appendix D.3 reports these robustness findings qualitatively.

E5.justification: v2 explicitly reports averaging simulations across multiple random seeds, matched seeds for aligned/gaming FL configurations, and qualitative seed robustness. v1 mentions coalition-sampling repetitions but not this cross-seed reporting practice. Exact run counts and empirical confidence intervals or error bars remain unspecified.

E6.justification: v2 replaces v1's result displays and adds stylized PoG of 0.658 and Fashion-MNIST PoG of 0.040. In Table 2, aligned-to-gaming head accuracy rises from 0.868 to 0.972 while tail welfare falls from 0.898 to 0.862. Figure 2 newly reports worsening welfare and participation as public weight decreases. These are new-setting results, not improvements over v1 scores.

T1.justification: Manipulability changes from constrained net-reward gain to a normalized metric/welfare-response ratio. The formal benign threshold becomes an upper cooperation limit, and global resilience replaces the earlier local indicator. v1's quadratic/KKT, identification, sample-complexity and hardness analyses are removed; v2 supplies new policy-level threshold and auto-switch propositions with proofs or sketches in Appendix A.

C1.justification: The contribution is redefined around the revised indices, an enforcement band preserving cooperation, and empirical estimation within a three-layer toolkit. v2 adds FL case-study claims and explicitly concludes that information design alone need not improve welfare. Its conclusion narrows v1's direct practical-applicability claims. PoC itself was already defined in v1.

C2.justification: v2 interprets reduced public-metric weight as potentially harming welfare and participation despite narrowing metric inflation, substantially qualifying v1's joint-reduction narrative. Section 8.2 and Appendix B add explicit discussion of normative welfare choices, fixed behavioral types, single-dataset evidence and unmodeled privacy mechanisms.

D1.justification: Reproduction instructions change from public version-pinned repositories, canonical release logs, hashes and shell commands to two described supplementary notebooks and a README. Appendices C–D add simulator, partitioning and CNN implementation information, although exact optimizer choice, layer widths, learning rates and batch sizes remain unspecified in the PDF. External artifact availability cannot be verified locally.

R1.justification: v2 retains the six related-work themes and most technical references, but removes the consulting-report citations and selected research citations, including Zrnic et al.'s strategic-classification sequencing work and Sundaram et al.'s PAC-learning work. It also adds more explicit positioning alongside existing aggregation and incentive mechanisms.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and discussion are extensively rewritten. Separate model, dynamics, coalition, mechanism and computational sections become metric, dynamics and toolkit layers followed by consolidated experiments. The lengthy extended discussion is replaced by reorganized proof, modeling and experimental appendices; the author list also changes.

P2.justification: v1's notation table and seven figure sets are removed and replaced by two numerical result tables and two multipanel bar-chart figures. The revision also changes typography, title/author arrangement, headers and page composition throughout. These are substantial display and layout changes beyond numerical updates or renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 improves empirical relevance through Fashion-MNIST and provides clearer organization and scope limitations. However, it replaces explicit local-model derivations with broader guarantees whose Appendix A sketches leave important details unresolved; the threshold proof explicitly leaves coalition rationality unformalized. Appendix D.2 also omits essential settings for the new experiment. These gains and verification weaknesses make the overall quality direction unclear.
